caption: The drawing is a grayscale technical illustration showing two views of a single object that resembles a bunch of grapes, each grape represented as a spherical bulge. The object appears metallic or stone-like due to the shading techniques used. On the left, there is a side view displaying a vertical column of round forms, capped at the top by a wedge-shaped element that extends horizontally to the right and ends in a serrated edge. To the right, there is a front view showing an irregular cluster of spheres arranged in a grape-like formation, with a short, angled protrusion ending in a rounded knob at the upper right. In the upper left corner of the drawing, there is a small inset diagram showing a labeled, dimensioned profile of the object, also in black and white. The composition is organized with the two main views centrally placed within a faint rectangular border, and the inset technical diagram is enclosed in a smaller rectangle that slightly overlaps the top left corner of the main border. The background is plain and off-white, with the artist’s name, James M. Lawson, and the designation “Del. - 186-1” noted in the lower right corner.
title: Iron Shutter Fastener
